meta.scenario: single vocal (T1 only) — T1 vocal active in outro, T2 instrumental; gradual mid suppression timed to fade_in start, standard 16-bar window

transition_arc: T1's vocal (Antony Hegarty) continues through the outro, echoing and tailing into near-silence around bar 88. T2 is purely instrumental deep house. Because only T1 has a vocal, a standard 16-bar blend is viable — no need to compress the window. But T1's mids must be suppressed at the moment T2 fades in so T2's groove establishes without the vocal competing for attention. The suppression is gentler than a dual-vocal scenario (mid=0.35 vs 0.2) because there is no competing T2 vocal — T1's voice becoming a soft background texture is acceptable. Standard bass swap at bar 88 (midpoint of 80–96).

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 72: 8 bars before T2 fade_in at bar 80. Vocal present (presence=6), groove still running, rms=0.34
annotated_actions.why: Bass pre-cut 8 bars before T2 enters. Mid stays at 1.0 — T1 should sound complete during these 8 bars. The mid suppression fires at bar 80 (when T2 actually arrives), not here.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 80: vocal active (presence=6), drums=0.22, harmonic=0.30, rms=0.28
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 16: T2 instrumental groove entering — no competing vocal
annotated_actions.why: Fires simultaneously with T2 fade_in. mid=0.35 (≈−5 dB broadband) — gentler than dual-vocal suppression because T2 has no competing vocal. T1's voice drops to a background murmur while T2's instrumental groove rises. The audience consciously hears T2 establishing; T1's voice becomes an atmospheric texture they're not attending to. high=0.9 retains T1's hi-hat character slightly (warmer than 0.8 because there is no hi-hat collision concern with one vocal track).
Kill T2 bass at fade start — prevents dual basslines during blend. EQ is persistent; will be restored at bass_swap point.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 16: instrumental intro, kick establishing, drums=0.35, harmonic=0.15
annotated_actions.why: 16-bar standard window. drums:0.7 (not 0.8) — slightly reduced because T1 still has an active groove with hats; combined percussion density would be high. other:0.6 — T2's pads are instrumental and same-key (9A=9A), zero harmonic clash, safe at 0.6. from_bar=16 skips T2's first 16 bars of near-silence. vocals:0.0 is a formality here since T2 is instrumental, but always set it explicitly. stems={drums:0.8, bass:0.0, other:0.6} — T2 enters with 80% drums, no bass (held for bass_swap), 60% atmosphere.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 88: vocal presence dropping (presence=3, tail phase), drums=0.12, rms=0.18
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 24 (from_bar=16, 8 bars elapsed): bass about to enter at bar 32
annotated_actions.why: Standard midpoint (80 + 8 = 88). T1's bass was cut via eq at bar 72. At mid=0.35 and 50% fade gain, T1's vocal is at roughly 15% of its original perceptual loudness — the ear has migrated its attention to T2's emerging groove. The swap releases T2's bass stem formally.
Restore T2 bass at bass_swap point — T1 bass is now HPF-cut, T2 bass can come in.
Simultaneous with T2 fade_in. Standard 16-bar fade_out. T1's mid-suppressed vocal fades gracefully. By bar 88, T1 is at 50% gain with mid=0.35 — audible only as a faint harmonic ghost.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 32: full instrumental groove, kick+bass+pads at full level, RMS 0.52
annotated_actions.why: T2 full mix fires. T1 gone. from_bar = fade_in.from_bar(16) + fade_in.duration_bars(16) = 32. T2's groove, teased through the 16-bar fade, arrives without any competing vocal. Clean handoff.
